extracted.intended_audience: public relations and marketing professionals, corporate communicators, and designers creating press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Practical design guidelines and best practices for creating visually effective press releases for digital and print distribution that align with brand and corporate communication standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey the theme with visual and aesthetic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A design that conveys the theme of its information is an essential aspect of PR; it should encompass visual and aesthetic elements that communicate news or information effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visuals, typography, layout and color to communicate the release’s theme; ensure visuals support the message and make the release memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate effective UI/UX design practices
rubrics_metrics.description: A persuasive press announcement involves a planned design approach and should incorporate effective UI design practices to ensure a user-friendly and intuitive interface that enhances the user experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize usability and intuitive navigation so readers can quickly find key information; apply UX principles for digital releases to improve engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readable typography / Choose professional fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Readable Fonts: Choose professional, easy-to-read fonts such as Arial or Times New Roman. The use of appropriate fonts is essential to press release design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep text professional and easy to read; select fonts consistent with brand identity and legible at common sizes for both print and screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent spacing and margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent Spacing: Use consistent line spacing and margins to ensure readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain regular line-height, paragraph spacing and page margins so readers can quickly process the information; avoid cramped layouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Hierarchy of Information: Use headings, subheadings, and bullet points to guide the reader through the most critical details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure content so the eyes naturally follow priority information (headline → lead → key facts → boilerplate); use typographic scale and visual weight to signal importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality, relevant images
rubrics_metrics.description: Images: One significant aspect is the use of images. Including high-quality, relevant images can capture the reader’s attention and convey the essence of the press release more effectively than text alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select photos and graphics that illustrate the news; ensure high resolution for print and appropriately sized files for web to avoid slow load times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visuals should reinforce content, not overtake it
rubrics_metrics.description: Images and Graphics: Use relevant images, charts, or infographics to enhance the message without overwhelming the text. The visuals should reinforce the content, not overtake it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance imagery and copy; avoid decorative visuals that distract from the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme and brand alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Theme: The theme should align with the branding and identity of the company or organization releasing the information. Consistent use of icons and symbols that reflect the brand’s image can help reinforce brand recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tone, imagery and color palette to the brand; use icons and symbols consistently across releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include brand identity elements (logos, colors, fonts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Branding: Include company logos, brand colors, and fonts to maintain consistency with corporate identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place logos and brand marks in predictable locations; apply brand color palette and approved typography to improve recognition and cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a grid system / clear structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: A grid system (a structured framework that lines up and organizes information for a consistent layout) can help maintain consistency. This makes the design visually cohesive and easier to navigate, enhancing readability and overall user experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a grid to align elements, create predictable reading flow, and ensure visual balance across sections and between images and text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic use of white space
rubrics_metrics.description: White Space: Use white space strategically to avoid clutter and ensure the content is easily digestible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give elements breathing room; avoid dense blocks of text to improve scanability and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align tone and style with corporate communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone and Style: Align the design with the company’s formal or casual tone, ensuring it reflects the corporate communication style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visually complement the language and messaging (formal vs. casual) to create a cohesive, professional presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and position a clear Call to Action (CTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Call to Action (CTA): Highlight key actions or responses that the press release aims to generate, such as visiting a website or contacting for more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place CTAs near the end, make them bold or visually distinct, use action-oriented copy (e.g., “Learn more”), and ensure clickable links for digital releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent, correctly formatted contact information and hyperlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperlinks and Contact Information: Ensure all links and contact information are easily accessible and correctly formatted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bold or contrasting colors for hyperlinks; place contact details in a clear, prominent section (header/footer); verify links and contact details before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize for digital and print (responsive and adaptable layouts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsive Design: Ensure the press release is designed for digital and print formats, adjusting for mobile and desktop viewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create layouts and assets that work across device sizes; prepare print-ready versions with suitable resolution and bleed where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEO-friendly layout and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: SEO-Friendly Layout: Design SEO-friendly headers, keywords, and meta descriptions to improve a website’s visibility in search engine results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear H1/H2 structure, include target keywords naturally, and supply meta titles/descriptions for online releases to increase discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive elements to enhance engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactive Content: Incorporating such elements as clickable infographics, videos, and animations helps engage readers and provides a vivid experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interactive features to let readers explore details dynamically, but ensure fallbacks for environments that don't support interactivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bold visuals and strong branding for memorability
rubrics_metrics.description: Bold Visuals and Branding: Large, eye-catching images and strategically placed brand colors help reinforce brand recognition and make the press release memorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hero images or prominent visual blocks to draw attention, while keeping balance with the copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean layout with clear navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean Layout with Clear Navigation: A clean and organized layout with straightforward navigation is crucial for readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intuitive navigation cues, consistent typographic styles and the grid system to help readers find key details quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visual storytelling techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual Storytelling: High-quality images, graphics, and other visuals make the overall effect impressive and the content more memorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange visuals and captions to tell the narrative of the announcement; sequence images to support the story flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile Optimization: As more users prefer reading from mobile devices, press release designs must be responsive and mobile-friendly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test readability, image scaling and CTA tap targets on mobile; simplify layouts for small screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimalist design to avoid clutter
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimalist Design: A clean, easy design with ample white space helps avoid clutter and makes the press release easier to read and navigate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize essential content, remove unnecessary decorative elements, and use restrained color and typographic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data visualization for complex information
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Visualization: Charts, graphs, and other data visualization tools help press release design be more informative and present complex information in an easily perceived format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose clear chart types, label axes and data points, and ensure visualizations are accessible and readable at intended sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media integration and sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Social Media Integration: Adding social media buttons and sharing options encourages readers to spread the word and increases the reach of the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include prominent share buttons, prewritten share text where appropriate, and images sized for social previews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use infographics to break up dense text
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate visual elements like infographics: Integrating infographics helps break up dense text, making content more engaging and easier to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert complex facts and figures into concise infographics to improve comprehension and retention; ensure they are on-brand and legible in both web and print formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor layouts separately for digital and print
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor the layout for both digital and print formats: Adapting layouts for both digital and print ensures optimal design across platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare distinct variations or flexible templates so the press release looks good in email/web, mobile, and printed collateral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent use of company brand colors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the company’s brand colors in the design: Using brand colors ensures consistency and strengthens recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply primary and secondary brand colors purposefully for hierarchy and emphasis; maintain contrast and accessibility for readability.
